# removed_in: # Vanilla template models that a release removed, and the model that took over their geometry.
# A mod model whose parent is the old template is pointed at the new one when the mod was built
# before removed_in and the host is removed_in or newer. Both columns name minecraft models.
# Each row was derived from the vanilla client jars: the old model exists in the last release
# checked before removed_in and in none from removed_in through 26.3, the new model exists in
# every one of those, and the two have the same elements with the same open texture slots.
# One name came back meaning something else. block/grass was the grass block in 1.12.2 and the
# short grass plant from 1.13 to 1.20.2, so it has a row for each meaning. Rows apply in release
# order: a 1.12 model's block/grass becomes block/grass_block at the 1.13 row, which the 1.20.3
# row, the plant's rename, then no longer matches.
# added_slots is "-" when the slots kept their names. Otherwise it lists new=old pairs: the new
# template reads slot "new" where the old one read "old", so the mod model gains "new": "#old",
# which also resolves when a child model is the one that sets "old".
